subject: Re: Availability apportionment for multi-tier latency spike
messages:
From: Alan Kelly <alan.kelly@cloudserve.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: sre@cloudserve.io
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected 30% latency increase 2026-09-18 22:50 UTC - evidence attached

Mina,

We're seeing a sustained 30% token-latency increase on our production path during the window below. Our probes indicate partial degradation concentrated on the east-2 edge cluster; we also observed your maintenance hash announced for 22:45 UTC but the degradation starts ~22:50 and persists for ~18 minutes beyond the maintenance window.

Timestamps (UTC):
- 2026-09-18T22:50:12Z: first latency spike noted
- 2026-09-18T23:08:35Z: measured traffic fallover to fallback region

Can you confirm how Redwood plans to apportion this against the SLA? CloudServe customers expect uptime credits when performance is meaningfully degraded and not attributable to our network.

Attached: edge-probe-logs-20260919.tar.gz (subset of our probe traces).

Thanks,
Alan Kelly
SRE Lead, CloudServe Inc.
alan.kelly@cloudserve.io
--
[Attachment: edge-probe-logs-20260919.tar.gz (logs, 12MB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Kelly <alan.kelly@cloudserve.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 30% latency increase 2026-09-18 22:50 UTC - evidence attached

Alan — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're pulling the serving runtime traces and our autoscaler events now. Preliminary notes:

- We had a scheduled kernel update that targeted a subset of east-2 GPUs; the announced maintenance window for that job was 22:40–22:50 UTC.
- Our internal metrics show an elevated tail latency beginning at 22:48 UTC and a partial KV-cache miss amplification between 22:50–23:06 UTC.
- The change in customer-observed latency appears to correlate with a re-routing event where ~12% of your traffic saw a longer remote hop.

We're going to run an apportionment calculation for partial degradation (weighting by request distribution and probe coverage). Ben — can you surface the draft calculation (SLO apportionment) and the probe overlap map? Marissa, can you check the maintenance job logs and whether the job extended past the announced end time?

I'll follow up with an initial determination by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
--
[Attachment referenced: none in this reply]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Kelly <alan.kelly@cloudserve.io>, sre@cloudserve.io
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 30% latency increase 2026-09-18 22:50 UTC - evidence attached

Team / Alan — attaching the first-pass SLO apportionment spreadsheet (slo-apportionment-draft-v1.xlsx). Summary:

- Total window: 2026-09-18T22:48:00Z -> 2026-09-18T23:08:00Z (20m)
- We estimate 11m of that time was full-path degradation (our side), 4m overlapped announced maintenance (22:40–22:50 UTC) where we claim exemption for the announced nodes, and 5m ambiguous where probe coverage is thin.
- For the ambiguous period we applied probe-weighted blending: 60% assigned to Redwood (serving runtime kernel update induced KV miss amplification), 40% to downstream network variance. That yields an effective apportionment of 74% Redwood-attributable within the total 20m window.

Notes / open items:
- CloudServe's probe coverage is denser on east-2 than our public probes; need to reconcile the probe sets to firm up the 5m ambiguous slice.
- If Alan can share a consolidated histogram of affected request distribution (e.g., ratio of chat vs. embeddings vs. reranking), we can reweight the apportionment by opcode cost.

Attachment: slo-apportionment-draft-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

-ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
--
[Attachment: slo-apportionment-draft-v1.xlsx]

From: Alan Kelly <alan.kelly@cloudserve.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, sre@cloudserve.io
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 30% latency increase 2026-09-18 22:50 UTC - evidence attached

Ben — thanks for the draft. A couple of points from our side:

1) Our telemetry shows the tail-latency delta affects primarily generation requests (chat paths) which represent ~78% of our Redwood traffic during that window. If you reweight by opcode cost that increases customer impact.
2) We ran an independent edge-synth test; the degradation appears to persist until 23:10 UTC (we can share the traces).
3) On the maintenance window: CloudServe did not schedule any changes on our side during 22:40–23:15; the only maintenance event we have is a peering policy refresh at 23:40 UTC, so this appears to be on your side.

Given the operational impact and the ambiguity window, we are asking Redwood to apply an expedited SLA credit and to treat at least the ambiguous 5m as Redwood-attributable pending final reconciliation.

Alan
Alan Kelly
SRE Lead, CloudServe Inc.
alan.kelly@cloudserve.io
--
[Attachment: cloudserve-synth-histogram-20260919.csv (12KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Kelly <alan.kelly@cloudserve.io>, sre@cloudserve.io
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 16:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected 30% latency increase 2026-09-18 22:50 UTC - evidence attached

Alan / team — final determination after cross-reconciling probes, kernel job logs and request opcode mix:

- We agree the customer-observed degradation window is 22:48–23:10 UTC.
- Maintenance exemption applies only to the nodes explicitly listed in the maintenance announcement; cross-check shows the kernel rollout was targeted at a different subset of hardware and completed at 22:50 UTC as scheduled.
- The majority of the residual tail amplification (22:50–23:10) is attributable to KV-cache miss amplification triggered by the kernel change; we therefore assign 80% of the 22:50–23:10 window to Redwood. The earlier 22:48–22:50 pre-rollout delta is ambiguous — assigned 50/50.

Net apportionment across the 22:48–23:10 window yields Redwood-attributable 68% of the degraded minutes. Per SLA Section 4.2, that attribution exceeds the threshold for a partial-degradation credit. We will process a credit equivalent to one week of usage-based credits applied to CloudServe's next invoice; detailed calculation attached and DocHub link provided.

Open items:
- Alan: please confirm receipt and whether you accept the credit calculation or want formal mediation.
- Ben: please drop the final workbook to DocHub and escalate to billing to queue the credit.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Reliability Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
--
[Attachment: slo-apportionment-final-20260921.xlsx (67KB)]
